item.title: China, Indonesia hold joint counter-terrorism training
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27
GUANGZHOU, Oct. 27 (Xinhua) -- The opening ceremony for the "Sharp Knife 2026" joint army counter-terrorism training between China and Indonesia was held in south China's Guangdong Province on Tuesday. Following the opening ceremony, troops from both countries are scheduled to begin specialized training in reconnaissance, communications, unmanned systems, sniping and counter-terrorism. This joint training is a planned military exchange between the two militaries for this year, aimed at improving their combat-oriented training capabilities. Troops from both sides are organized into mixed groups to jointly conduct specialized sub-training, tactical coordination and comprehensive drills. The two sides will also engage in thematic seminars, weapon and equipment displays, sports competitions and cultural exchanges. This joint training focuses on joint counter-terrorism rescue operations in mountainous regions, involving mountain climbing, special vehicles driving, helicopter rappelling, close-range assault, and coordinated operations between manned and unmanned systems, according to an earlier statement issued by China's defense ministry. The statement noted that the joint training, as the third edition of this series, will help further deepen practical exchanges and cooperation between the two militaries and enhance both sides' joint operational capabilities. The joint training is scheduled to run until early November, the statement added.

item.title: 6th Chinese Peacekeeping Helicopter Contingent to UNISFA completes equipment rotation mission
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27
By Huang Hao, Wu Xinwei, Wang Binwen, Yang Jiewei and Bian Haoyu A new helicopter attached to the 6th Chinese Peacekeeping Helicopter Contingent to UNISFA touches down at the airfield of the UNISFA Smart Camp. ABYEI, Oct. 27 -- Two peacekeeping helicopters painted with "UN" marking and the Chinese national flag landed smoothly at the airfield of the UNISFA Smart Camp on October 26, 2026, marking the successful completion of a transnational helicopter rotation mission by the 6th Chinese Peacekeeping Helicopter Contingent to the United Nations Interim Security Force for Abyei (UNISFA). Spanning 21 days, the mission required personnel to transit across two countries, one region, and three airfields and airports, covering a total flight distance of over 2,300 kilometers. Two new helicopters attached to the 6th Chinese Peacekeeping Helicopter Contingent to UNISFA touch down at the airfield of the UNISFA Smart Camp. Chinese peacekeepers assigned to the 6th Chinese Peacekeeping Helicopter Contingent to UNISFA remove the main rotor blades of an outgoing helicopter. Chinese peacekeepers assigned to the 6th Chinese Peacekeeping Helicopter Contingent to UNISFA remove the tail rotor blades of an outgoing helicopter.

item.title: Xi orders all-out rescue efforts after 7.0-magnitude earthquake in Xizang
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23
BEIJING, Oct. 23 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has ordered all-out search and rescue efforts for the missing and prompt medical treatment for the injured after a 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck a county in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region on Thursday night. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, urged in an important instruction every effort to minimize casualties. The earthquake struck Baqen County in Nagqu City, Xizang, at 10:33 p.m. Thursday. The quake has left 16 people dead and 65 injured, according to local authorities. Noting that the affected area is at a high altitude with low temperatures, Xi stressed the need to closely monitor seismic activity and weather conditions to prevent secondary disasters. Efforts should be made to properly accommodate the affected residents, repair damaged infrastructure as quickly as possible, and safeguard people's lives and property, Xi said. Premier Li Qiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, called for solid disaster prevention and response efforts. The Ministry of Emergency Management and authorities in Xizang have mobilized resources for rescue and relief operations.

item.title: Only by thoroughly reflecting on its past and sincerely repenting can Japan truly face the future: Defense Spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
BEIJING, Oct. 16 -- "Only by thoroughly reflecting on its past and sincerely repenting can Japan truly face the future," said Senior Colonel Chen Xi, spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense (MND), at a press briefing on Friday. The spokesperson made the remarks when commenting on the war crimes of the notorious Unit 731 of the Imperial Japanese Army. According to reports, the Singaporean documentary Inside Unit 731: Japan's Secret Human Experiments received Singapore's national award for the Best History Documentary, with 1.45 million views on YouTube. Japan Broadcasting Corporation (NHK) aired the documentary A Secret Unit: The Silent Postwar Era, which exposes Unit 731's crimes against humanity through newly discovered photographs, firsthand testimony and other evidence. The spokesperson pointed out that during World War II, the Unit 731 conducted appalling humane experiments and waged biological warfare in China. These heinous crimes gravely violated international law. The extent of their crimes against humanity is beyond description, marking one of the darkest chapters in the history of human civilization. He further noted that right-wing forces in Japan have recently used emerging technologies to "poison" data in an attempt to whitewash Japan's culpability for its aggression and distort public perceptions, once again triggering high vigilance within the international community. "As some insightful people in Japan have pointed out, historical truth cannot be erased, and the crimes committed by the Japanese forces during their invasion of China are backed by irrefutable evidence and cannot be denied," stressed the spokesperson.

item.title: China Will Take Effective Measures to Deter Any Sabotaging Moves in South China Sea: Defense Spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
BEIJING, Oct. 16 -- "The Chinese side will take resolute and effective measures to deter any sabotaging moves in the South China Sea, and uphold regional peace and stability," said Senior Colonel Chen Xi, spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense (MND), at a press conference on October 16, 2026. According to media reports, the Philippine side recently made provocations near Huangyan Dao and Ren'ai Jiao multiple times and said that it would not allow the Chinese side to dictate terms on Philippine "territory". The Philippine military claimed that they observed over a hundred Chinese warships and China Coast Guard vessels maintaining regular presence in waters near Zhongye Dao and Xianbin Jiao, and that the Chinese side intended to shake the Philippines' resolve in safeguarding its rights and interests. "China has indisputable sovereignty over Huangyan Dao and Nansha Qundao, including Zhongye Dao, Xianbin Jiao and Ren'ai Jiao, and their adjacent waters, and has sovereign rights and jurisdiction over relevant waters," said the spokesperson. The spokesperson pointed out: "These islands and reefs lie outside the scope of Philippine territories. Therefore the Philippine side is not qualified to claim 'safeguarding its own rights and interests'." "The Chinese side takes necessary measures in accordance with laws and regulations to uphold its sovereign rights. They are legitimate, reasonable, professional and standardized," the spokesperson added. "For some time, the Philippine side has been rallying external forces to stir up troubles in the South China Sea at the expense of the common interests of regional countries. It continues to make provocations violating others' sovereignty and distort facts to spread false narratives, which makes itself a destroyer of peace and a destabilizing factor in the South China Sea," the spokesperson noted.
